name: the spellplague
lore:
### **Codex Entry: The Spellplague (The Blue Breath of Change)**

To the uninitiated, magic is a tool; to the scholar, it is the lifeblood of the cosmos. In the **Year of Blue Fire (1385 DR)**, that blood turned to poison. The Spellplague was not merely a disaster; it was the violent unraveling of reality itself.

#### **History: The Night the Weave Frayed**
The cataclysm was ignited by the deicide of Mystra, Mother of All Spells, at the hands of the Mad God Cyric and the Nightmistress Shar. With her demise, the Weave—the lattice through which all mages draw power—shattered. A torrent of raw, unrefined arcane energy, manifesting as cerulean flames, tore across the planes. It consumed empires, rearranged the stars, and forced our world, Toril, to partially merge with its long-lost twin, Abeir.

#### **Significance: A World Rebuilt**
The aftermath was total. Archmages were driven to madness, their spells manifesting as sentient horrors. Geography became fluid; mountains took to the sky as "motes," and seas drained into the Underdark. Most harrowing was the "Spellscar"—a brand borne by survivors that granted erratic, flickering power at the cost of one’s physical stability or sanity. The very laws of thaumaturgy were rewritten, leaving magic a wilder, more treacherous mistress.

#### **Legends and Lore**
Folk tales speak of the **Blue Breath**, a sentient mist that still haunts the wild places, seeking to "change" those it touches. Some cults worship the Plague as a purifying fire, claiming it purged the "stagnant" old world. Yet, for the seasoned adventurer, it remains a grim reminder: when the Goddess dies, the world screams in blue fire, and nothing—not even the earth beneath your boots—is guaranteed.
